name: Ōgetsuhime
depicted_variant: Reverent painterly crop-origin event: two tall sheaves surge from closed eyes, heavy golden rice sheds grain under gravity; three silkworms spin silk at crown beside two cocoons.

visual_requirements.description: One serene deceased female deity with closed eyes and fully opaque layered robes; no wounds, exposed body or decay.
Two dense rice sheaves physically arise from both closed eyes; a few unmistakable silkworm caterpillars emerge at crown, spinning silk beside cocoons.

aura: Reverent awe comes from powerful crop-origin miracle c05, with low view and real grain falling under gravity, never aura or invented soil power.
artistic_choices: Dense tall ripe rice sheaves and upward low perspective amplify the literal rice-from-eyes c05 miracle, without enlarging goddess or inventing body attributes.
Falling ripe grain is editorial gravity-driven motion; ground remains still, no soil magic is depicted.
Only three pale silkworms at crown, fine silk and two cocoons are editorial natural silkworm staging to make c05 unmistakable and prevent decay/maggot reading.

Plain ancient Japanese layered ivory/russet robes and broad hand-painted serene dignified features are editorial respectful presentation, not claimed costume history or photographic present-day model.
Other c05 body crop origins omitted for clear reverent composition; no Susanoo, wounds, resurrection or aura.
prompt:
ONE original square premium PAINTERLY cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Ogetsuhime, ancient Japanese food goddess at the overwhelming birth of rice and silkworms from her body after death.
ANATOMY: ONE dignified adult female deity with one head, two CLOSED eyes, two arms and two covered legs, reclining deceased with no injury, no wounds and no blood. Serene solemn idealized features of an ancient goddess, NOT a photographic modern woman, no modern makeup. Ancient-period Japanese layered robes, plain fully opaque ivory over muted russet underlayers, high crossed neckline, long sleeves, closed hem. Loose long black hair. Clothing is editorial, no unsupported crown or symbols. [ogetsuhime-c01,ogetsuhime-c04,ogetsuhime-c05]
MOMENT: SURGE UPWARD from BOTH CLOSED EYES as TWO DENSE TALL SHEAVES of living RICE. The rice stems visibly originate at each closed eye without wounds, then thrust high above the viewer into dark night. Bend huge masses of HEAVY GOLDEN RICE EARS outward under their own weight. Countless real ripe RICE GRAINS shake loose from the bowed ears and FALL DOWNWARD in a vigorous shower, passing in front of robe and landing on dark ground. The canopy of fresh grain seems to have just unfolded, an immense event of new life, not a motionless bouquet. [ogetsuhime-c05]
SILKWORM DETAIL: only THREE unmistakable plump pale SILKWORM CATERPILLARS at the CROWN OF HER HEAD, one visibly SPINNING FINE SILK threads onto TWO clean pearly oval COCOONS nestled together at her crown. Clear intact caterpillar heads and soft tiny legs, never dozens of grubs or maggots, never insects scattered on soil. Delicate silk catches the same shaft of light. No decay. [ogetsuhime-c05]
POWER: crop-origin miracle c05 ONLY. Rice physically surges from both eyes, silkworms arise at head. Falling grains are ordinary gravity acting on ripe ears, editorial physical motion. NO MOVING OR LEVITATING SOIL, no ground magic, glowing particles, aura, resurrection or living spellcasting.
SCALE & CAMERA: EXTREME LOW ground-level view beside her head looking UP into the two towering sheaves, normal human body and rice scale enlarged through perspective. Her head and covered shoulders occupy lower half of frame, both eye-origin points clear; tall curving stalks and golden ears fill upper half and loom overhead. A covered forearm and relaxed five-fingered hand on lower right, second arm recedes along covered body, no extra limbs. Crop miracle belongs unmistakably to this deity, never a field or still life.
LIGHT & WEATHER: ONE STRONG SHAFT OF WHITE MOONLIGHT falls diagonally through black night onto sheaves, face and fine silk. Bright golden physical grain against deep walnut darkness, dramatic shadows, sharp rim on falling seed. No visible full moon needed, no soft photographic beauty lighting.
SURFACE: visibly hand-painted broad irregular brushstrokes and textured pigment throughout, especially face and robe. Inspired by painted narrative legend rather than a photograph or 3D render. Heavy woven layered cloth, brushy black hair, fibrous green rice stalks, dense ripe gold ears, clean pale silk and two cocoons.
SETTING: dark neutral earthen ground, no architecture or invented ritual setting. Ground stays still, scattered grain falls onto it.
MOOD: REVERENT MAJESTY, overwhelming abundance and life emerging after death, sacred awe of a living Shinto tradition; never horror, decomposition, sleeping modern woman, cute or calm decorative tableau.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: NO photographic skin, modern woman portrait, worms on earth, decay, wounds, blood, gore, exposed body or sexualized view. No Susanoo, weapon, crown, flower bouquet, text, letters, logo, border, frame or watermark. No aura, neon, energy ribbon, light motes or soil magic. No extra heads, eyes, arms, legs or fingers. No borrowed film/game/anime/comic design.
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

rejected_attempts.reason: Keep: the c05 crop-origin miracle after her death (c04), non-graphic. Closed eyes; no wounds, blood, gore or exposed body; a fully opaque robe; rice from both eyes and silkworms from her head; no Susanoo and no aura. Fix: (a) Make the miracle a powerful event, not a still life. Dense rice stalks surge up out of both eyes in two tall sheaves that rise high above her into the night. Heavy golden ears bend and shed grain that falls like rain onto the dark earth, and the soil around her stirs. Use a low, ground-level camera beside her head so the rice towers over the viewer, with one strong shaft of light on it. Optionally add the other non-graphic c05 origins (millet from the ears, azuki beans from the nose) as small, clear details. (b) Silkworms: a few unmistakable pale silkworm caterpillars emerging at the crown of her head, spinning fine glinting silk with a cocoon or two, so they read as silkworms being born. Not many grubs scattered across her hair and the soil. (c) Paint her in the house painterly style as an ancient Japanese goddess, in ancient-period layered robes (editorial) with serene, dignified features, not a photographic modern young woman. Reverent and majestic, never horror. No text.

visual_review.notes: Native1254,200 and silkworm/cocoon crop inspected: one serene deceased deity, closed eyes, opaque layered ivory/russet ancient robe editorial, clearly hand-painted textured features and cloth rather than photographic modern woman. Two dense tall rice sheaves emerge from both closed eyes c05, bow overhead and shower real golden grain downward under gravity; low ground view makes crop-origin event imposing at200. A few pale silkworm caterpillars at crown visibly spin fine silk beside TWO clean cocoons; none scattered on soil, no decay reading. One foreground five-fingered hand clear, other arm recedes in robe; lower legs outside crop, no visible extra limbs. No wounds/gore/exposed body, Susanoo, aura or soil magic. Reverent sacred abundance and active grainfall answer Claude static-life critique. Seven Sangar checks pass; entire prior Claude reject archived.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face/eye-origin, crown/silkworm (left and right, zoomed), hand and robe/body crops. This redraw answers the r01 reject. One adult goddess (ogetsuhime-c01) lies dead (c04), with one head, two closed eyes and a serene closed mouth, and no wounds, blood or decay. She is painted in visible impasto brushwork as an ancient goddess, not as a photographic modern woman. Her layered ivory-over-russet robes are fully opaque, with a crossed collar and long sleeves (editorial), and no body is exposed. One hand is visible at lower right, resting on the soil with natural relaxed fingers and no extra digits; the other arm recedes under the robe, and there are no extra limbs. Rice is born from her eyes (目から稲, c05): two dense sheaves spring directly from the closed eyes with no wound. They rise high overhead and bow under heavy golden ears that shed a shower of grain onto her robe and the dark earth (ordinary gravity; the ground stays still, with no soil magic). Silkworms are born from her head (頭から蚕, c05): four or five unmistakable pale, segmented silkworm caterpillars with dark eye-spots and prolegs sit at the crown, one rearing up and spinning fine silk onto two pearly cocoons. None are scattered on the soil, and they read as silkworms, not maggots. The receipt says three; the extra one or two are harmless editorial staging, since c05 gives no number. An extreme low, ground-level camera beside her head and one diagonal shaft of cold moonlight against walnut darkness make the rice tower over the viewer. At 200px it reads as a sacred crop-origin miracle with grain raining down: reverent and awe-inspiring, fitting a living Shinto tradition, not a sleeping woman, horror or a still life. No Susanoo, aura, text, border or borrowed design. The other c05 origins are left out by choice, which keeps the scene modest.
